title: Globex SSO kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Globex SSO (R-01, R-05, R-06). To hit the Q1 deadline with one identity engineer (K-03), the team locked D-16: buy SAML and SCIM through WorkOS instead of building it, R-16: SCIM deprovisioning also revokes every API key the user created, and T-03: Lena runs a WorkOS spike against Globex's Okta sandbox. EU residency (Q-03) stays open.
utterances: Globex renewal is in March and SSO is the condition. SAML plus SCIM, live by end of Q1. Lena, you're leading.
Honestly, building SAML ourselves is two to three months for me alone, and SCIM on top. That's the whole quarter.
What about WorkOS or Auth0? Both do SAML and SCIM as a service.
WorkOS fits better, it handles Okta and Entra and gives us SCIM webhooks. Rough estimate is three weeks of integration.
About 125 dollars per connection per month. Against an 800k renewal that is noise.
My worry is lock-in on login.
We keep our own user and session model. WorkOS only does the IdP handshake and directory sync, so we can swap it later.
Okay. Proposal: we buy SAML and SCIM through WorkOS, we don't build it.
One security thing: when someone is deprovisioned, their API keys keep working today.
Good catch. SCIM deprovisioning has to revoke every API key that user created, not just the dashboard login.
And EU residency? Globex wants that too.
Separate problem, still open. Lena, first a WorkOS spike against Globex's Okta sandbox this week.
I'll have a working SP-initiated login by Friday.

locks.text: Buy SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0 through WorkOS instead of building them; Northwind keeps its own user and session model so the provider stays replaceable.
SCIM deprovisioning must revoke every API key the removed user created, not only their dashboard login.
Lena runs a WorkOS spike against Globex's Okta sandbox and demos a working SP-initiated SAML login by Friday, November 13.
